subject: Career
title: The Burnout-Depression Overlap
description: Learn The Burnout-Depression Overlap in one minute.

hook.text: Is she burned out or depressed? The symptoms overlap. Getting the diagnosis wrong means getting treatment wrong.

buildup.text: Burnout and depression share fatigue, hopelessness, and withdrawal. But they have different roots and treatments.

discovery.text: Burnout is context-specific: change the job and it often resolves. Depression is pervasive across all areas of life.

twist.text: Untreated burnout can evolve into clinical depression. The line between them blurs over time.

climax.text: If burnout symptoms persist outside work — in hobbies, relationships, weekends — seek professional evaluation.

punchline.text: Burnout is situational. Depression is pervasive. Know the difference.

quiz.question: How does burnout differ from depression?
options: Burnout is context-specific; depression pervades all areas of life

details.summary: Burnout and depression share symptoms like fatigue, hopelessness, and difficulty concentrating, yet they are distinct conditions. Burnout is context-specific to work, while depression pervades all life domains. The overlap makes misdiagnosis common and complicates treatment approaches.
details.whyItMatters: Confusing burnout with depression leads to inappropriate treatment. Understanding the distinction helps people seek the right support, whether workplace changes for burnout or clinical treatment for depression.
takeaways: Burnout is work-specific; depression affects all areas of life
Roughly 20 percent of burnout cases co-occur with clinical depression
Correct identification determines effective treatment strategy

faq.question: How can someone tell if they have burnout versus depression?
faq.answer: The key differentiator is domain specificity. If symptoms lift on vacation or weekends, burnout is more likely. If low mood, worthlessness, and disinterest persist across all life contexts regardless of work absence, depression should be evaluated clinically.

faq.question: Can workplace burnout actually cause clinical depression?
faq.answer: Research shows sustained burnout can trigger clinical depression in vulnerable individuals. Chronic emotional exhaustion depletes neurological resilience over time. Early burnout intervention reduces the risk of progression to depression significantly.
